memos.scout:
Honest case for buying Cassie now: thin. The strongest signals are real but mixed.

For: 1,314 buyers and 4,623 buyers in the last 15 minutes is broad participation, not a handful of wallets. Top-3 holders are only 6% of the curve and the top-5 buyer share post-graduation is 14%, so no single entity dominates the flow. The coin is alive, 30 minutes old, and has held up off its high, with net flow slightly positive over the last 15 minutes (+108 SOL) at a 47% return.

Against, and more heavily: the last 15 minutes show 3,134 SOL sold against 3,242 bought, a near-even churn, which means the rally is being distributed to new buyers rather than absorbed. The 30-minute return of 7.3x means most early holders are sitting on large gains, and the 22% drawdown from the high is already happening. The sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes after graduation was 0.91, and a launch bot was present. The completer holds 62% of the curve, which is a concentration risk that the top-3 figure hides. Round-trip costs of 1.4-5.1% would also consume much of any short-term bounce.

Verdict: no strong case for entry. Demand exists, but it is churning at the top of a run, and the brief lacks evidence it
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss path is distribution into the post-graduation bid. The coin is up 7.3x in 30 minutes, but the last 15 minutes show $3,241 SOL bought against $3,133 SOL sold, with net flow of only 108 SOL on about 3,000 SOL of two-way volume. Sellers (3,885) outnumber the buyer count of the window's exit side, and sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes after graduation was 0.91. The completer holds 61.7% of the curve, and the bundle share is 27%, so insiders hold a large block that can exit into any strength. The 21.8% drawdown from the 30-minute high means the top may already be in. With $263 SOL pool depth, a $20 round trip faces 1.4 to 5.1% in fees and impact, so a move needs a sustained rally to pay. Nothing here supports a buy. Skip.
